name: AS-REP Roasting (Rubeus)
description: Request AS-REP responses for accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled and crack them offline. No credentials required.

recommended.note: CPTS card for cracking AS-REP hashes

notes: Roastable = DoesNotRequirePreAuth=True. Can also be set via GenericWrite/GenericAll for targeted attack.

defense.why_it_works: Kerberos pre-authentication forces clients to encrypt a timestamp with the user's key before the KDC issues a TGT. When pre-auth is disabled (DoesNotRequirePreAuth = True), the KDC returns an AS-REP containing data encrypted with the user's hash — without requiring any authentication. An attacker sends an AS-REQ for the target account and receives the crackable ciphertext without knowing the password.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to DC on port 88. At least one domain account with DoesNotRequirePreAuth = True (or no domain account at all — AS-REP roasting works unauthenticated when the list of vulnerable accounts is known). Rubeus /asreproast or impacket-GetNPUsers.
defense.impact: T1558.004 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: AS-REP Roasting. Obtains crackable ticket for accounts with pre-auth disabled. Completely unauthenticated if target account is known. Success rate depends on password strength.
defense.detection:
Event 4768 (TGT Request) with Pre-Authentication Type = 0 (no pre-auth) — legitimate users always have pre-auth type > 0. MDI 'AS-REP roasting' alert. Bulk 4768 requests from a single source with different cnames. Zeek Kerberos: AS-REQ without encrypted timestamp.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4768 with PreAuthType=0 from unexpected source | MDI alert: 'AS-REP roasting attack' | Zeek kerberos.log: AS-REQ with no enc-timestamp | SIEM: multiple 4768 PA-Type=0 from single IP
defense.prevention:
Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts (default; audit for exceptions). Use Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} regularly and remediate. MDI deployment. Long passwords on any account that must have pre-auth disabled (legacy compatibility).
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Unauthenticated attack — can be launched from outside the domain. Single request per target account — minimal noise compared to Kerberoasting. Use Rubeus /nowrap for clean output.
defense.misconfiguration: Accounts created with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' checked — often legacy service accounts or misconfigured automation accounts. No periodic audit for this attribute.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Accounts vulnerable to AS-REP roasting:
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth
# Output: svc_legacy — DoesNotRequirePreAuth: True → VULNERABLE

# Can be exploited without any credentials:
# Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:svc_legacy /format:hashcat /outfile:asrep.txt
# → $krb5asrep$23$svc_legacy@CORP.LOCAL:... (crack with hashcat -m 18200)
